significance: A walled complex of gates, terraces, pools and shrines on a plateau about 3 km south of Prambanan, identified with the Abhayagiri Vihara, the monastery on the hill free from danger. Occupied through the 8th and 9th centuries, it mixes Buddhist remains such as an Avalokitesvara shrine, Dhyani Buddhas and an Akshobhya effigy with Hindu ones including a lingam and yoni, Durga, Ganesha and Garuda.
story: Javanese folklore makes the plateau the palace of King Boko, whose daughter Loro Jonggrang set Prince Bandung Bondowoso to raise a thousand temples in a night, then had the village women pound rice so the cocks would crow early, for which the prince turned her to stone.
